description: Interactive: draws your answer as a card the reader can use, from an A2UI v0.9.1 document you write: a comparison of options with a verdict, a plan as steps or a timeline, a cost or sizing calculator with sliders and a chart that follows them, a quiz or flashcards, a table, a Mermaid diagram. Call it whenever the answer has a shape: the reader asks to compare ("compare", "X vs Y", "pros and cons", "trade-offs", "which is better for"), for a plan ("plan", "roadmap", "migration steps", "rollout", "timeline"), to "show me", "explain how", "draw", "chart" or "visualise" something, or for "a table of" options, rather than answering with a long Markdown table or list. A concept explore_concept knows, a decision decide has a tree for, and a cost estimate_cost prices go to those tools first. For a Databricks question, first get the facts with search_guide or get_chapter, put them in the document, and pass those URLs as sources: only pages of the Field Guide are listed as sources, and the card is labelled "Composed by your assistant". In a host that renders MCP Apps it opens as an interactive card; the text result renders the whole document, so it is complete without the view. Nothing is stored and no model is called; a document that won't draw comes back as the spec's VALIDATION_FAILED list to fix (the tool checks the document's structure, not its facts).

document.description: An A2UI v0.9.1 document: messages as JSONL, one a line (createSurface, updateDataModel, updateComponents), or a JSON array of them. Use Fabric's catalog (https://agents.fabric.pro/a2ui/v0.9/fabric_catalog.json: the basic catalog plus Chart, Stat, Callout, Steps, Quiz, Flashcards, Timeline, Compare, Diagram, Code, Table; functions calc and formatValue) or the basic one. Exactly one component has id "root".

sources.description: The Field Guide URLs (with #anchor) whose facts the document uses, from search_guide or get_chapter. Each is checked: a page of the guide is cited as a source; anything else is listed as not from the guide.

title.description: The card's title, in plain words
